documents.title: User stories — Usage inventory → parity/parity.yaml (S00)
documents.body:
# User stories — Usage inventory → parity/parity.yaml (S00)

## Personas

- **The programme owner** — signs `parity/parity.yaml`; the signature is the gate that every `used` id will be built and every `dropped` id will not.
- **Every delivery slice** — consumes `parity_ids` from the one inventory instead of deciding its own scope.
- **S14 acceptance** — gates on 100 % of `used` ids.
- **S13 flow re-authoring** — consumes the n8n tuples and the named flows.
- **The inventory session (S0)** — measures the four systems read-only and writes the contract artifact.
- **The platform office** — keeps the schema, the signed SUMMARY and the project record.

## Stories

- As the programme owner, I want one signed inventory of the fr, RM, Planka and n8n surface, so that zero-usage surface is dropped rather than ported (SPEC §8 S0; D2/R5).
- As a slice lead, I want stable `parity_ids`, so that my slice builds only what is used and cites the id it satisfies.
- As S14, I want every `used` row to carry an acceptance string, so that 100 % of used surface is tested.
- As S13, I want the distinct `(package, resource, operation)` tuples and the named flows, so that the flow re-authoring covers exactly the live n8n surface.
- As the inventory session, I want five evidence classes with a fixed precedence A > B > C > D > E, so that `used` is defensible where logs are thin.
- As the platform office, I want a closed schema and an executable gate, so that the inventory is checked, not trusted.

## Scenarios

- Given the four sources (fr 785 served operations, RM 314 decorators, Planka 67 openapi paths, n8n 348 workflows / 332 active), when steps 1–6 run, then every surface is normalised to `METHOD /path`, `<package>.<resource>.<operation>` or a flow name and given one `P-NNNN` id.
- Given an active caller (class A), when a row is classified, then it is `used` and a Loki zero never downgrades it.
- Given a B-only row, when it has fewer than 5 hits in either 24 h sample, then it is not `used`.
- Given a decision-dropped surface, when an active caller hits it, then the run stops as a contradiction instead of choosing silently.
- Given a `dropped` row, when the gate reads it, then its `evidence` starts with `decision:` or `replacement:`.
- Given the signed inventory, when the drop list was executed, then migration 0011 removed the 7 already-built zero-usage tables and their 24 actions (registry 177 → 153).

## Verify

- Slice §7, G1–G7: ids unique, id shape exact, `used` acceptance valid, every surface exactly once, dimensions equal, two samples, dropped reason present.
- `check-jsonschema --schemafile parity/schema.json parity/parity.yaml` — the closed 9-key schema validates.
- `yq 'length' parity/parity.yaml` — 1300.
- `python3 scripts/check-parity.py` — the public file matches the signed sha256.
- `parity/SUMMARY.md` — `signed_off`, the hash, counts per area × status and the gate output.
- `docs/evidence/rework/S00.json` — verdict green at snapshot 7f0df874.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md` §1–§11.
- Artifact: `parity/parity.yaml`, `parity/schema.json`, `parity/SUMMARY.md`.
- Record: seed project S00; `docs/evidence/rework/S00.json`; `acceptance/programme/S00.toml`.

## Notes

Reconstructed from the plan and the signed SUMMARY on 2026-11-28 for standard v4; the inventory was signed 2026-11-08 and the project re-closed green on 2026-11-26. This is the Delivery narrative the standard asks for, not a new claim.

documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria — Usage inventory → parity/parity.yaml (S00)

## Scenarios

- The inventory holds one row per surface — 1,300 in all: fr 798, rm 314, planka 96, n8n 92.
- Every id is unique, matches `P-NNNN` and is never reused; a dropped row keeps its id.
- Every `used` row carries `test:<crate>::<name>`, `e2e:<spec>::<name>` or `probe:<METHOD> <path>`.
- Every `dropped` row names its reason: `evidence` starts `decision:` or `replacement:`.
- Every B-class `used` row has at least 5 hits in each of the two 24 h Loki samples — the operative G6 assertion (G6 as written only counted files).
- Every surface appears exactly once, and the parity row count equals the union of the four manifests.
- The schema is closed (`additionalProperties: false`, 9 required keys) and every row validates.
- `parity/SUMMARY.md` carries the signed block, the sha256 and the counts per area × status.
- The recorded status mix is 218 `used`, 295 `rare`, 543 `unused`, 244 `dropped`; evidence classes A 173, B 66, D 1061.
- The zero-usage decision was executed, not only written: migration 0011 removed 7 built tables and 24 actions (registry 177 → 153).
- The project closed through the one gate: charter approved, baseline approved, board-approved delivery contract with a distinct approver, compliant Phase-G review citing the standing delegation, closure gate decided by a distinct approver, 0 waivers.

## Verify commands

- `yq 'length' parity/parity.yaml` — 1300 (G5).
- `yq -r '.[].id' parity/parity.yaml | sort | uniq -d` — empty (G1).
- Each of the 1,300 ids matches `P-NNNN` — 0 bad (G2).
- `yq -r '.[] | select(.status == "used") | select(.acceptance | test("^(test|e2e|probe):") | not) | .id' parity/parity.yaml` — empty (G3).
- `diff <(cat parity/surfaces/*.txt | sort -u) <(yq -r '.[] | [.app, .surface] | @tsv' parity/parity.yaml | sort)` — empty (G4).
- `yq -r '.[] | select(.status == "dropped") | .evidence' parity/parity.yaml | grep -Ev '^(decision:|replacement:)'` — empty (G7).
- `check-jsonschema --schemafile parity/schema.json parity/parity.yaml` — ok.
- `shasum -a 256 parity/parity.yaml` and `python3 scripts/check-parity.py` — the signed hash.
- `yq -r '.[] | [.area, .status] | @tsv' parity/parity.yaml | sort | uniq -c` — the SUMMARY count table.

## Results

Met and signed. `parity/parity.yaml` holds 1,300 surfaces: 218 `used`, 295 `rare`, 543 `unused`, 244 `dropped` (classes A 173, B 66, D 1061). G1–G5 and G7 passed, the schema validated, and G6 was replaced by its real assertion — all 24 B-class `used` rows have at least 5 hits in each sample. The SUMMARY is signed off as georgedekker on 2026-11-08 (recorded by the agent on owner instruction), sha256 `2d7b93c56a07703ffb4293d9425f447339e151a09a036771d2d708ae7786e4e8`; the public file was sanitised on 2026-11-12 (ef8302b, 2c51115) with ids, counts and statuses unchanged. Migration 0011 executed the drop list. The project re-closed green on 2026-11-26 at snapshot 7f0df874.

## Status

met — the inventory is signed, schema-checked and enforced by `scripts/check-parity.py`; S14 gates on 100 % of `used`.

## Links

- Plan §7 (gate), §9 (classification), §11 (closed decisions).
- Artifact: `parity/SUMMARY.md`, `parity/schema.json`, `parity/parity.yaml`.
- Record: `docs/evidence/rework/S00.json`.

documents.body:
# Definition of ready — Usage inventory → parity/parity.yaml (S00)

## Independent

S00 has `depends_on: []` and changes no table, action, event or module (plan frontmatter: `adds_tables`, `adds_actions`, `adds_events` and `adds_modules` are all empty). The measurement is read-only against four running systems; the only write is the new `parity/` tree. No other slice writes it; every slice reads it.

## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed — one signed inventory and zero-usage surface dropped, not ported. The method was settled at delivery: five evidence classes, precedence A > B > C > D > E, two 24 h Loki samples with a positive control per zero, and five open questions each carrying a stated default.

## Valuable

S00 removes the named gap: without a measured inventory a rework ports surface on guesswork, and features can be built before the inventory that should have gated them. It maps to SPEC §11 R5 / D2 — zero-usage surface is dropped, not ported — and gives every slice its `parity_ids` and S14 its 100 % `used` gate. The seven tables built before S00 and then dropped by it are the measured cost of the gap.

## Estimable

The plan names 15 steps of at most one day each, every source query and every pin: fr@4a579e91d355, rm@191086942ce5, kanban@aafb771cea4c, n8n 348 workflows / 332 active. The starting counts are measured (785 served fr operations, 314 RM decorators, 67 Planka openapi paths) and the acceptance is executable.

## Small

One slice, one artifact set — `parity/parity.yaml`, `schema.json`, four surface manifests, the evidence files and `SUMMARY.md` — with no code tables, actions, events or modules. The measurement is read-only; the only follow-on change is the recorded drop migration.

## Testable

Slice §7 is an executable gate over the artifact (G1–G7 plus the schema); every `used` row carries an acceptance string; the signed sha256 is enforced by `scripts/check-parity.py`; the project-level check is the S00 acceptance manifest.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: none — `depends_on: []`.
- blocks: every slice that consumes `parity_ids`; S14's 100 % `used` gate.
- related: SPEC §4, §8 S0, §9, §11 R5; the four source systems (fr, RM, Planka, n8n).
- external reads: master Postgres for row counts, Loki for traffic, the n8n database for workflows and executions — read-only, never through PgBouncer.

## Notes

Reconstructed for standard v4 on 2026-11-28 from the plan and the signed record; the project's closed state is the record's.

documents.body:
# Definition of done — Usage inventory → parity/parity.yaml (S00)

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Verify |
|---|---|
| One row per surface, each exactly once; ids unique and `P-NNNN` | G1, G2, G4, G5 |
| Every `used` row carries `test:`/`e2e:`/`probe:` acceptance | G3 |
| B-class `used` justified by at least 5 hits in each of the two samples | the operative G6 assertion; `parity/evidence/surface-counts-sample1.tsv` and `surface-counts-sample2.tsv` |
| Every `dropped` row starts `decision:` or `replacement:` | G7 |
| The closed schema validates | `check-jsonschema --schemafile parity/schema.json parity/parity.yaml` |
| The file matches the signed hash | `python3 scripts/check-parity.py`; `parity/SUMMARY.md` |
| The drop list was executed, not just written | migration 0011: 7 tables and 24 actions, registry 177 → 153 |
| The project closes through the one gate | `docs/evidence/rework/S00.json` — verdict green |

## Evidence at completion

`parity/parity.yaml` (1,300 surfaces), `parity/schema.json`, `parity/surfaces/{fr,rm,planka,n8n}.txt`, `parity/evidence/` (preflight, day-2 method, two surface-count samples, executions, row counts, Keycloak clients, matches, reclassification), and `parity/SUMMARY.md` signed on 2026-11-08 with sha256 `2d7b93c56a07703ffb4293d9425f447339e151a09a036771d2d708ae7786e4e8`, sanitised on 2026-11-12. The project record is green at snapshot 7f0df874e7c26681ee36923b5c17e76a99254b24: charter approved, baseline approved, delivery contract board-approved by an approver distinct from the requester, Phase-G review compliant and citing the standing delegation, closure gate decided by a distinct approver, 0 waivers, 1 WBS node with the four WSJF inputs, and 1 accepted deliverable with a demo credit.

## Repo gate

The plan §7 gate is the repo gate: G1–G7 as assertions, then `check-jsonschema --schemafile parity/schema.json parity/parity.yaml` and `scripts/check-parity.py`. `check-jsonschema` was absent on 2026-11-07 and was installed with `uv tool install check-jsonschema`. No Rust compile is involved in S00; the repository's preflight and PR CI remain the compile and lint verdict for the campaign branch.

## Merge and closure

S00 carries no issue list — the plan is its build record. The artifact set landed in the tree and the inventory was signed on 2026-11-08; acceptance was recorded on the project row. The project closed through the one gate: closure review published, closure gate decided by an approver distinct from the requester, and the verdict re-checked green on 2026-11-26. The plan §5 sign block — `signed_off`, date and sha256 — is in `parity/SUMMARY.md`.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md` §5, §7.
- Artifact: `parity/parity.yaml`, `parity/SUMMARY.md`.
- Record: `docs/evidence/rework/S00.json`; `acceptance/programme/S00.toml`.
